title: Platform degradation explainability and root-cause attribution standard
author: Marcus Liu
content:
Overview
=======
This document defines a standardized platform-level approach for detecting, explaining, and attributing service degradations across Redwood Inference. The goal is to produce concise, actionable explanations for oncall and engineers that: (1) identify the degraded surface (latency, errors, quality, cost), (2) provide a ranked set of likely root causes, (3) link to reproducible queries/dashboards, and (4) recommend immediate mitigations and next steps.

Audience
--------
Platform operators, service owners, oncall engineers, SREs, and product engineers responsible for inference SLAs and runtime health.

Scope
-----
Applies to all platform-hosted control plane services and inference serving paths (api-gateway, router, caching, runtime, kv-cache, batching, model-host). Does not replace deep model quality analysis in Applied ML — it provides attribution signals that feed the model quality pipeline.

Standards Summary
-----------------
- Signals to capture (minimum): p50/p95/p99 latency, request success rate, token-cost-per-request, token-emitted-rate, model-variant-usage, batch-size distribution, KV cache hit ratio, GPU-utilization, pod_eviction_count.
- Standard alert names and thresholds (examples):
  - platform.degradation.latency.p95.service: p95 > configured SLO * 1.3 for 5m (severity: P2)
  - platform.degradation.errors.rate.service: error_rate > 0.5% and > 2x baseline 5m (severity: P1)
  - platform.degradation.kvcache.hitratio.service: kv_hit_ratio drop > 25% vs 1h baseline (severity: P2)
- Explainability outputs must include: impacted routes, temporal window, prioritized probable causes (top 3), confidence score (low/medium/high), required artifacts (queries, span traces, synthetic test).

Telemetry contract (required fields)
----------------------------------
| metric_name | retention | granularity | ownership | notes |
|-------------|-----------|-------------|-----------|-------|
| latency_ms   | 90d       | 10s         | runtime-team | label: route, model_id, tenant_id, model_variant |
| request_count| 90d       | 10s         | api-team     | status_code, route, tenant_id |
| kv_hit_ratio | 30d       | 30s         | runtime-team | prefix, tenant, region |
| gpu_util_pct  | 365d      | 60s         | infra-team    | node_id, pool_id |
| token_cost_per_req | 365d | 1m          | billing-team  | estimated_cost_usd |

Detecting a degradation
-----------------------
1) Alert fires or synthetic detects deviation.
2) Auto-enrichment service (degrade-explain) captures the incident window (default 15m before alert to 30m after) and collects required telemetry slices.
3) Create a triage card in the platform incident board with auto-populated fields (impact, SLO, snapshots).

Attribution heuristics (ordered)
--------------------------------
1) Surface correlation: correlate primary symptom (e.g., p95 latency) with candidate signals via time-series cross-correlation (Pearson r) and change-point alignment.
2) Dependency amplification: check upstream/downstream error spikes (gateway, auth, model-host). Increase probability when dependent service error rate increased within ±2m.
3) Resource exhaustion: test whether GPU or host-level metrics (cpu steal, load, memory pressure) exceed historical 99th percentile.
4) Workload shift: identify sudden changes in tenant mix, model-variant or batch-size distributions > 3x baseline.
5) Configuration changes & rollouts: search recent deploys, feature flags, or kernel switches in last 60 minutes.
6) Regression tests: run targeted synthetics (sample prompt set) against the previous stable model/variant to check quality regressions.

Each heuristic contributes weighted evidence. The explainability service summarizes top 3 causes with normalized confidence (example: ["kv-cache-threshold-liable", 0.72], ["host-thermal-throttle", 0.54], ["tenant-burst", 0.33]).

Required dashboards and views
----------------------------
- Degradation Overview (global): p95/p99 heatmap by route, service, and region (time range: last 12h).
- Attribution Canvas (per-incident): timeline with overlays for alerts, deploys, config changes, and top-correlated signals.
- Tenant Impact Slice: top 10 tenants by req count and cost during incident window.
- Resource Lens: GPU and host-level metrics, eviction events, node-level logs.
- KV-cache probe: hit ratio timeline with prefix-level drilldown.

Example PromQL and SQL snippets (for dashboard panels)
-----------------------------------------------------
PromQL (p95 latency for route):
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route=~"/v1/(generate|chat).*"}[5m])) by (le, route, model_variant))

SQL (tenant impact):
  SELECT tenant_id, count(*) AS reqs, sum(estimated_token_cost_usd) AS cost_usd
  FROM telemetry.requests
  WHERE ts BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB('%INCIDENT_START%', INTERVAL 15 MINUTE) AND TIMESTAMP_ADD('%INCIDENT_END%', INTERVAL 30 MINUTE)
  GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY cost_usd DESC LIMIT 10;

Operator triage procedure (step-by-step)
---------------------------------------
1) Open the incident card from the alert and confirm the impacted SLO and services.
2) Run the auto-enrichment job (button: "Populate Explainability Snapshot").
3) Review Attribution Canvas and top-3 causes.
4) Execute targeted synthetic: run 10 queries against suspected model_variant and a control variant. If latency difference > 2x or error delta > 5% escalate to runtime oncall.
5) If evidence points to configuration or deployment, roll back via the release manager (see rollout checklist).
6) If resource exhaustion, trigger emergency scale policy (scale-up GPU-pool) and attach remediation ticket.
7) Document root cause and mitigation in the incident board and link to RCA document.

Automation hooks and APIs
------------------------
We provide an internal explainability microservice (degrade-explain) with a simple API:

POST /v1/explain
Content-Type: application/json
body example:
{
  "incident_id": "INC-2026-000123",
  "service": "model-host-prod",
  "start": "2026-02-10T01:12:00Z",
  "end": "2026-02-10T01:45:00Z",
  "symptom": "latency_p95",
  "threshold": "1200ms"
}

Response (trimmed):
{
  "incidence_window": "2026-02-10T01:12:00Z/2026-02-10T01:45:00Z",
  "top_causes": ["kv-cache-eviction-spike","tenant-burst","node-throttle"],
  "confidence": ["high","medium","low"],
  "attachments": ["/dashboards/degradation/INC-2026-000123" ]
}

(Known caveat: response schema is evolving; avoid programmatic dependency on exact keys — prefer the attachments and top_causes).

Escalation mapping and ownership
--------------------------------
- P1 (service error-rate > 2x baseline or consumer-visible failure): notify service owner, runtime oncall, infra oncall. Pager duty escalation: service-owner -> runtime -> infra.
- P2 (degradation in latency or cache hit ratio): notify platform-operator rotation and service-owner.
- P3 (minor SLI drift): create a ticket for next business day triage.

Service-level SLO examples (for attribution purposes)
----------------------------------------------------
- api-gateway: 99th success rate 99.95% monthly, p95 latency < 200ms for short requests.
- model-host (interactive): p95 token-latency < 1200ms per request for 512-token median workloads.
- kv-prefix-cache: hit ratio >= 70% for warm workloads (30d window).

Post-incident deliverables
-------------------------
Every explainability-enabled incident must produce:
- Short summary (1–2 paragraphs) with top cause and immediate fix.
- Attachments: canvas screenshot, top-5 queries used, synthetic run output.
- Owner-assigned follow-ups with deadlines and signal to monitor.

Quality controls and tooling improvements
---------------------------------------
- Quarterly review of attribution precision: select 10 incidents, run manual RCA and score platform attribution accuracy. Target: >= 80% top-1 precision.
- Add unit tests for heuristic modules and example datasets in the explainability repo.
- Maintain a library of synthetic suites (latency, error, quality) per model family.

Appendix: quick checklist for oncall
------------------------------------
1) Confirm alert and incident window.
2) Run enrichment and open Canvas.
3) Check deploys/feature-flag timeline.
4) Inspect GPU/node metrics and eviction events.
5) Run 10 synthetic probes (control vs suspect).
6) Apply mitigation: rollback, scale, circuit-break, or tenant-throttle.
7) Update incident card and notify stakeholders.
